newsitem.title: UK: Sears extends losses after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Sears extends losses after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Sears extended their losses, tumbling 7-1/2p, or eight percent, to 84p, after the UK retailer said it expected its full year earnings to be significantly below those of last year.

The UK retailing group, whose pre-tax profits were 100.1 million stg in the last fiscal year, said its same store sales in the Christmas period were down by a disappointing 0.5 percent against a year ago, though like for like sales in the second half to January 6 were up one percent.
The shares were down before the trading statement as the Guardian newspaper reported on Thursday that Sears would issue a profit warning.
The newspaper said some institutional investors were planning a campaign to remove chief executive Liam Strong.
Separately, Sears also confirmed that it is in advanced negotiations with the Littlewoods Organisation regarding the sale of Freemans mail order business. The move was widely expected by the market.
